system.summary: Homophonic substitution of 22 letters with 51 signs (up to four for S; the digits 7-11 serve as A, E, I, O, V), 41 two-digit word and syllable codes in first-letter order, ten name signs and three doubling signs (Lasry's key, lasry2022/ctts/key.txt).
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's 'Louis XIII-Sabran cipher (1631)'; Baluze 156 f. 157 (1636) probably the same, not covered
system.notes: Clerks' hands differ: the '6' shape is H and the straight b is F in the 1631 key and the ff. 215/232 hands, but the clerk of ff. 57 and 242v-245v writes H with a straight stem and F as a script L. distinct_symbols counts transcription labels, which include hand variants.

prior_solution.where: George Lasry's 2022 key and his decipherment of Baluze 155 f. 79 (images on Tomokiyo's GL.htm); the fr. 4134/4135 passages unpublished until this contribution, apart from a partial AI reading of nine fr. 4134 leaves (issue #56, 20 Oct 2026). No edition found.

conditions.human_role: Contributed result (PR 84): George Lasry transcribed in CTTS and recovered the key with CTTS's built-in cryptanalysis (2022), and in October 2026 completed the transcription and the nomenclator with Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI Codex and edited and translated the letters. Here: merge, mechanical and statistical checks, comparison with the earlier contributed reading, one-line image spot-check.

solution.what: [former entry sabran1631] Fetched the DECODE record view for R2748 and its four images (Gallica scans of Baluze 155 f. 79-80) with the shared cookie.

[former entry sabran1631] Checked Tomokiyo's louisxiii.htm (DECODE's pointer) and GL.htm: R2748 solved by George Lasry in 2022, key and decipherment as images; the same cipher in Sabran's letters, fr. 4134 and fr. 4135. Entry closed without applying the key.

[former entry sabran1631] Split from the former combined target louis1615 (catalogue 191) under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R2748 (the 1631 Sabran cipher, Lasry's solution) and R2785/R2786 (the Brulart de Leon cipher of 1615-18, Tomokiyo's key) are different ciphers. Folder, profile, page and ledgers separated; earlier steps kept as recorded. Lasry's three GL.htm images fetched to summarise the content.

[former fr. 4134 entry] Outside input, issue #56 (Harumi-Matsuba): AI transcription of the cipher passages of nine fr. 4134 leaves (891 signs) by Claude Opus 5.5, disagreements judged by Codex and Claude Sonnet over seven rounds (16 of 60 corrections reverted on a two-way re-judging).

[former fr. 4134 entry] Outside input, issue #56: Lasry's 2022 key applied to the transcription; 879/891 signs valued; words on every leaf (Savone, munitionnaire, prisonniers, donner la place, de l'intelligence dans cet estat), long stretches without words on ff. 50v, 54r, 57r.

[former fr. 4134 entry] Outside input, issue #56: 1000 shuffled keys scored on French-likeness, 0 at or above the real key on every leaf; independent Codex transcription (three runs) 92.4-92.7% sign agreement; calibration on Baluze 155 f. 79 against Lasry's decipherment 92.0% of letters.

[former fr. 4134 entry] Re-measured here (measure.py): fr-1600-letters LM beats all 1000 shuffled letter keys on every leaf; 666/896 decoded letters (74.3%) covered by corpus words of 3+ letters against 27.0% median for shuffled keys; calibration recomputed 551/599 (final) and 540/599 (first transcription).

[former fr. 4134 entry] Gallica (BnF IIIF) images of f. 66r and f. 66v compared sign by sign with the contributed transcription: f. 66v 59/59, f. 66r 113/116 checked signs agree; a duplicated '8 nt' across c139_23/23b and a wrong AI-agreed correction z->lh (c139_23c, secre[t]) found.

[former fr. 4134 entry] No DECODE record for fr. 4134 or fr. 4135; Tomokiyo louisxiii.htm/GL.htm list the passages as undeciphered and credit Lasry with finding that the key applies; Lasry to be asked whether he holds readings.
George Lasry transcribed Baluze 155 f. 79 (Louis XIII to Sabran, 1631) in CTTS (date from his key sheet 'BNF Francais 4134', 25 May 2022, published on Tomokiyo's GL.htm).

CTTS's built-in cryptanalysis recovered the homophonic letter table (22 letters, up to four signs each) from the 1631 letter; Lasry found that the same key reads Sabran's letter-books fr. 4134 and fr. 4135.

George Lasry (PR 84), with Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI Codex: all 43 images in CTTS (Baluze 155 a1-a2, fr. 4134 ff. 46v-73v, fr. 4135 ff. 132-252); clear text transcribed, 144 missed cipher signs added, double boxes split (supposed codes 98, 72, 82 = 9+8, 7+R, 8+R), sign types reviewed against the images for each clerk's hand.

Nomenclator completed from context with Claude Opus 5.5: 41 two-digit word codes in first-letter order (17 bon, 24 ce, 26 de, 35 Genes, 47 monsieur, 59 que, 68 vous), ten name signs read tentatively ([France?], [Espagne?], [Republique?], [Savoie?] ...), three doubling signs; code 46 unknown.
George Lasry edited and translated 18 letters (lasry2022/READING.md): the Monaco talks of 1631 and 1635, the Savona plot of 1633 (Garbarino of Sassello), Genoa's neutrality in the 1635 campaign.

Merged here: decode.py re-applies lasry2022/ctts/key.txt to the CTTS transcription and reproduces Lasry's counts exactly: 3,353 signs, 2,853 letter signs, 287 firm and 212 tentative codes ([Traicte] counted tentative), 1 unknown (46). Baluze 155 528 signs, fr. 4134 1,061, fr. 4135 1,764; 108 distinct sign labels.

coherence.py: 83.7% of the deciphered text (letters plus firm word codes) falls in French words of 3+ letters (Baluze 155 91.6%, the ceiling on Lasry's fully deciphered letter; fr. 4134 84.5%; fr. 4135 80.8%); shuffled letter keys median 36.9%, max 44.9%.

Compared with the independent AI reading of nine fr. 4134 leaves (Harumi-Matsuba, issue #56): 761 of their 865 decoded letters align with Lasry's (88%; f. 73v 100%, f. 66v 98%, f. 50v 77%, where theirs formed no words). Their unlisted codes 35, 12, 33 are Lasry's Genes, [Agent?], [Guerre?]. One cipher line of Baluze 155 f. 79r checked on the DECODE R2748 image: all 26 signs agree.

No edition of the fr. 4134/4135 cipher passages found (web search, Tomokiyo louisxiii.htm and GL.htm, the contributor's sources); Sabran's 1636-37 despatches printed in the Correspondance de Sourdis are later. The former entries sabran1631 (Baluze 155) and the fr. 4134 entry merged here under the one-key rule.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 2853 tokens, 52 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.125 per letter; random keys -5.728 (z 7.8); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.239 (mean -3.255, z 94.3); annealer on the real text -2.916. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.125; polyphony 0.0; 354 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.916

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry recovered the letter table from the 1631 letter with CTTS's built-in cryptanalysis (2022) and completed the nomenclator from context with Claude Opus 5.5 (2026); no clear copy or outside key was used.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode.py --counts: 3,352 of 3,353 cipher signs in the 43 images carry a value (code 46 unknown); 212 code readings are tentative. Word cover (coherence.py) 83.7% against a 91.6% ceiling on Lasry's fully deciphered 1631 letter. Leaves of the same key not among the images are open (see gaps).
